notes: PSA 13.5 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.45. Prostate volume 30 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.89.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for rising PSA and prior prostate cancer diagnosis to discuss treatment options.

Recently retired mechanical engineer with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed via biopsy in 2022 (Gleason 3+3) and 2024 (Gleason 3+3). PSA has risen steadily from 4.8 ng/mL in September 2022 to 13.5 ng/mL in January 2025. Patient lives with partner, exercises by running 3x/week, and consumes 3 units of alcohol weekly. Comorbidities include hypercholesterolaemia (on atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin), obesity, and osteoarthritis. Ex-smoker (36 pack-yr, quit 2017). No recent bone pain or haematuria. Dermatology follow-up for actinic keratosis check completed recently.

On DRE, a nodule is palpated in the mid right transition zone, consistent with cT2a staging. General examination reveals stable vital signs (BP 116/79 mmHg, HR 68 bpm) and no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly.
